page: Microsoft Azure D4ls_v7 is an x86_64 architecture server instance belonging to the Dlsv7 family, virtualized via Microsoft Hyper-V. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel Xeon 6973P-C cores, running at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The processor includes a 480 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, though it is premium storage capable.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-threaded performance, with gzip compression reaching 34.6 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 14.78 GB/sec. However, multi-core and multi-threaded operations show relative weakness, as evidenced by a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 4513.8 and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 28.69 GB/sec. Memory performance is average, with a read-only small block bandwidth of 335.78 GB/sec and a large block write bandwidth of 23.19 GB/sec. The system supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), which assist in workloads like small-scale LLM inference, where it achieves 155.95 tokens/sec for text generation on a 135M model, though performance drops significantly on larger 7B models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D4ls_v7 offers a specialized hardware profile that trades memory capacity for dedicated high-frequency CPU cores. This makes it a resource-dense option for compute-bound tasks that do not require large memory footprints. Appropriate workloads include single-threaded processing, static web serving (benchmarked at 8.6 GB/sec), lightweight database operations, and basic utility hosting. It is less suitable for memory-intensive applications, large-scale multi-threaded processing, or complex machine learning inference.

It is configured with 8.0 GB of memory, resulting in a low-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per core, and lacks local storage or integrated GPUs. Single-core performance is strong, highlighted by high gzip compression and bzip3 decompression speeds, though multi-core scaling and write bandwidth are relatively weak.
